subject: Request: exclusion workflow & evidence package for LLM model-improvement (VitalHealth)
messages:
From: Maya Torres <maya.torres@vitalhealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: privacy@vitalhealth.com, procurement@vitalhealth.com
Date: 2026-11-01T14:03:00-05:00
Subject: Data use exclusions / evidence for model improvement

Karthik,

Thanks for taking this. VitalHealth’s procurement team is putting the final DPA together and we need a clear, auditable path showing how customer data — specifically PHI/patient-identifiable content and any prompts containing clinical notes — can be excluded from LLM model improvement pipelines. Can you confirm the following items and provide a sample evidence pack we can review with our security/compliance team: 

- Contractual commitment to exclude flagged data from any model training/updates (scope, account-level or dataset-level).
- The operational workflow: how flags are captured (API/UI), where excluded data is routed/stored, retention policy, and deletion SLA.
- Current list of subprocessors (including region of processing) and whether any subprocessors may transfer data outside the US.
- Example evidence artifacts you can provide at time of signature or upon request (subprocessor snapshot, audit log extract, signed attestation).

We have a target procurement window of mid-November and would like to close the DPA quickly if the evidence lines up with our requirements. Can you also indicate whether Redwood provides an API-level no-train toggle for accounts and whether prompt/response outputs are considered customer IP (we need ownership assurances)?

Appreciate a short summary and any materials you can attach.

Best,
Maya Torres
VP, Security & Privacy
VitalHealth

--
Attachment: procurement_checklist.xlsx (stub)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Maya Torres <maya.torres@vitalhealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, procurement@vitalhealth.com, privacy@vitalhealth.com
Date: 2026-11-02T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Data use exclusions / evidence for model improvement

Maya —

Thanks for the clear list. High level summary up front: Redwood supports account-level and route-level "no-train" opt-outs; when enabled we exclude flagged inputs and derived outputs from model improvement pipelines and persist only minimal metadata for billing/traceability. We can provide a bundled evidence package at signature plus periodic snapshots on request.

Quick bullets to address your asks (details and attachments below):
- Contractual commitment: we can provide an amendment to our standard DPA that adds a no-train commitment scoped to an account ID and to specific environment labels (prod/stage). We use a tagging model so you can apply opt-out by account or by route.
- Operational workflow: flags can be set via API header (X-Redwood-No-Train: true) or via Console toggle. Flagged traffic is routed to a segregated processing path that disables model-improvement hooks, prevents writes to improvement queues, and sets a 30-day retention counter for cached artifacts.
- Subprocessors: attached is our current subprocessor snapshot (subprocessors_current.csv) with region columns. We will provide a signed snapshot at time of signature and a 30/60/90 day update cadence if required.
- Evidence artifacts: we’re attaching a no-train evidence template that outlines the attestation, sample audit extracts (log lines), and a subprocessor export. We can also deliver a hashed-audit extract that shows request IDs and timestamps without exposing prompt content.

I’ve looped in Laura (legal) and Rishi (security) to confirm the contractual language and the audit artifacts. We’re happy to do a short technical deep-dive this week to walk your security team through the exact artifacts.

Attached: DPA_redwood_vitalhealth_redlines.pdf (draft redlines), subprocessors_current.csv, no_train_evidence_template.docx

Proposed next step: 30-minute call with your security + procurement to review the evidence template and finalize the scope (account vs route). Do mornings PST work?

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0183

--
Attachment stubs: DPA_redwood_vitalhealth_redlines.pdf, subprocessors_current.csv, no_train_evidence_template.docx
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Maya Torres <maya.torres@vitalhealth.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, procurement@vitalhealth.com, privacy@vitalhealth.com
Date: 2026-11-03T11:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Data use exclusions / evidence for model improvement

Maya —

Looping in from Legal. A few clarifications on scope and the types of deliverables we can commit to in contract: 

1) Scope of no-train opt-out: Redwood can accept account-level opt-outs (applies to all ingestion tied to the account ID) and per-route opt-outs (applies to a specific API key/route). We can include both options in the DPA amendment; the operative scope will be defined by account ID or route name in the schedule.

2) Evidence at signature: we can provide the following at signing: 
  - Signed subprocessor snapshot (CSV) identifying processing locations and subprocessors.
  - A signed attestation describing the segregation controls for no-train traffic and the retention/deletion policy.
  - A sample (redacted/hashed) audit extract showing request IDs, timestamps, and processing flags.

3) Prompt/response ownership: Redwood’s standard position is that customers retain ownership of prompts and generated outputs. We will include explicit IP language in the DPA amendment confirming customer ownership of prompts and model outputs generated from your account.

4) Cross-border transfers: subprocessors in our roster include cloud providers that may have processing in multiple regions. We will include a transfer schedule and can commit to limiting processing to US regions for the no-train path where feasible; any transfers will be documented in the subprocessor snapshot and subject to SCCs or equivalent.

5) Operational SLAs: for deletion we can commit to acknowledging deletion requests within 48 hours and to completing deletion of caches/derivatives from the no-train path within 30 days. Longer timelines may apply for backups — we will include backup handling language in the amendment.

I have added redlines to the attached DPA draft (see DPA_redwood_vitalhealth_redlines.pdf). Once you confirm scope (account vs route) we can finalize the schedule and the exhibit that enumerates the evidence deliverables and delivery cadence.

Thanks —
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

Laura / Karthik —

Thanks for the quick responses. A couple of follow-ups from our side before the call: 

- Prompt/response IP: appreciate the confirmation on ownership. Please confirm whether any telemetry or hashed identifiers are retained for caching purposes (e.g., hashed prompt IDs or embeddings). We need to ensure hashes cannot be reversed and are excluded from improvement pipelines when the opt-out is active.

- Evidence granularity: the redacted/hashed audit extract sounds good. For procurement we will need the following at signature: attestation, subprocessor snapshot, and a sample audit extract covering a 7-day window. Is that feasible?

- Deletion SLA: 30 days for caches/derivatives is acceptable provided we receive a signed attestation confirming backups are treated consistently or provide a backup retention carve-out.

- Cross-border / processing location: our security team prefers that no-train traffic be constrained to US-only processing. If that isn’t feasible for some subprocessors, please indicate which subprocessors will process no-train traffic outside the US.

- API/UI controls: we also need to see your Console UI for the no-train toggle or an API swagger for the X-Redwood-No-Train header so our platform team can instrument calls.

If you can confirm the above and provide the 7-day sample audit extract, we’ll move to DPA review with legal and aim to sign within two weeks.

Best,
Maya

--

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Maya Torres <maya.torres@vitalhealth.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, procurement@vitalhealth.com, privacy@vitalhealth.com
Date: 2026-11-05T16:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Data use exclusions / evidence for model improvement — technical details and artifacts

Maya —

Thanks for the follow-ups. Technical answers and commitments below, and I’ve attached the subprocessor CSV and the evidence template for your security team to review.

1) Retained telemetry / hashes: we store a small set of metadata for billing and tracing. For no-train traffic we will not persist raw prompt or response content to model-improvement stores. We do persist request IDs and a salted SHA-256 hash of the prompt for cache-keying; the salt is rotated periodically and held in HSM. The hashes are not reversible and are excluded from any training datasets when the no-train flag is present.

2) Sample audit extract: we can generate a 7-day redacted sample that contains: request_id, timestamp, route, processing_flag (no-train=true/false), and processing_region. No prompt text or generated output will be included. We’ll deliver the sample as CSV with a signed attestation.

3) No-train path processing location: the segregated no-train path is routable to US-only instances where feasible. The subprocessor CSV flags which subprocessors have US-only processing options and which have multi-region footprints. If VitalHealth requires a strict US-only guarantee for no-train traffic, we’ll document which subprocessors cannot comply and propose options (e.g., dedicated private deployment or a specific Dedicated capacity pool).

4) Deletion and backups: primary caches and KV artifacts in the no-train path are purged within 30 days of deletion request. Backups are on a 90-day rotation by default; we can add language to the amendment that allows an accelerated backup purge for no-train accounts subject to reasonable operational constraints.

5) Audit logs and evidence: attached is the no_train_evidence_template.docx that enumerates the extract fields, signing authority, and delivery cadence. We can commit to producing the signature-ready evidence at time of DPA signature and provide monthly snapshots on request.

6) API/UI toggle: Console has a per-account toggle (Settings -> Security -> No-train opt-out) and the API header is X-Redwood-No-Train: true. We’ll share the swagger snippet in the drive link and can demo the Console toggle on the call.

Next step: we can prepare the 7-day sample audit extract within 3 business days after we receive a non-prod account identifier from you to generate realistic logs. If you prefer not to share a test account we can provide a scrubbed historical sample.

Let us know which option you prefer and we’ll schedule the technical deep-dive.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Director, Security Engineering
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

--
